narrative:

This high probability indicates significant concerns about your preparedness for the exam, which ultimately led to the rejection of your application.

The most influential factors in this prediction were your academic performance in your third year and your first year, as well as your LSAT score. Your ranking in your third year placed you in the lowest decile, while the average for accepted students was notably higher. This suggests that your academic performance may not align with the expectations of successful candidates. Similarly, your first-year ranking was also at the bottom, indicating a consistent pattern of lower academic achievement compared to your peers.

Your LSAT score, while slightly below the average for accepted students, also contributed negatively to the prediction. This standardized test is a critical measure of readiness for law school, and your score reflects a challenge in meeting the benchmarks set by other applicants.

Given these insights, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance and preparing more thoroughly for standardized tests. Consider seeking additional support, such as tutoring or study groups, to enhance your skills and knowledge. Strengthening these areas could significantly improve your chances of success in future applications and on the bar exam.
